notes:
The typescript turns to “Interprétations en termes de filtrations du foncteur oubli” and compares filtrations of a fixed conjugacy class with parabolics, and cocharacters of that class with pairs (P,L) consisting of a parabolic and a Levi subgroup. It describes the class through M/W and a Weyl-chamber representative, then displays the two maps from ST_c and (CL)_c' to the filtration/parabolic schemes. The last paragraph restricts to characteristic zero, defines Dyn_c, changes torseur to espace homogène, and begins the definition of Un_c, which continues onto the next selected scan.

The author writes “j'ignore dans quelle mesure c'est vraiment nécessaire” immediately after the characteristic-zero assumption. The stabilizer addition asks “il faudrait regarder la structure de ces Z_o; dimension, semi-simplicité”. These are explicit source uncertainties, distinct from editorial doubts about letters. The previously typed identification of Dyn_c with an Isom(G_1,G) torsor is cancelled. No reason for the cancellation is inferred.

Actual checks, separate from reading: naturality of the filtration under inclusions/projections proves that it respects direct sums; consequently it is exact on split exact sequences. This checks the mechanism of the inserted exactness remark conditionally on semisimplicity of the representation category. Complete reducibility in characteristic zero remains a background input. For GL(V), assigning fixed weights to the summands of a split flag directly recovers a cocharacter and its block diagonal centralizer, giving a concrete check of the Levi-splitting correspondence, without proving the general scheme or descent statements.

For Sl₂ acting on k²⊕k inside SL₃, the exact centralizer computation gives diag(t,t,t⁻²), a one-dimensional torus. Its Lie algebra is spanned by diag(1,1,−2). This supplies one answer to the author's question: the stabilizer need not be semisimple. For G=SL₂×SL₂ and f(s)=(s,1), the conjugacy orbit has dimension 3, while an Isom torsor has dimension 6; thus the explicitly cancelled torsor identification fails in that example. The three bracket relations give a three-dimensional derivation algebra for sl₂, and perfectness kills cross-factor derivations, supporting the dimension comparison; faithfulness of the group differential is a stated background input.
